==English==
{{wp}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ten-}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|contenten||to satisfy}}, from {{der|en|la|contentus#Etymology_2||contained; satisfied}}, past participle of {{m|la|continēre||to contain}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|kəntĕnt'}}, {{IPA|en|/kənˈtɛnt/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-content (verb).wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛnt|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|con|tent}}

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|more,er}}

# {{senseid|en|satisfied}} [[satisfied|Satisfied]], [[pleased]], [[contented]].
#* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=I|text=This new-comer was a man who in any company would have seemed striking.{{...}}He was smooth-faced, and his fresh skin and well-developed figure bespoke the man in good physical condition through active exercise, yet well '''content''' with the world's apportionment.}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun|-}}

# [[satisfaction|Satisfaction]], [[contentment]]; [[pleasure]].
#: {{ux|en|They were in a state of sleepy '''content''' after supper.}}
#* {{RQ:Wollstonecraft Mary|passage=‘It is very difficult to {{...}} learn to seek '''content''', instead of happiness.’}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-2|act=I|scene=i|passage=Such is the fullness of my heart's '''content'''.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[acquiescence|Acquiescence]] without [[examination]].
#* {{RQ:Pope Essay on Criticism|passage=The sense they humbly take upon '''content'''.}}
# That which contents or satisfies; that which if attained would make one happy.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-2|act=1|scene=i|passage=So will I in England work your grace's full '''content'''.}}
# {{lb|en|UK|House of Lords}} An expression of [[assent]] to a [[bill]] or [[motion]]; an [[affirmative]] [[vote]].
# {{lb|en|UK|House of Lords|by metonymy}} A member who votes in [[assent]].

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{senseid|en|satisfy}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To give contentment or satisfaction to; to satisfy; to make [[happy]].
#: {{syn|en|elate|hearten|Thesaurus:gladden}}
#: {{ux|en|You can't have any more. You'll have to '''content''' yourself with what you already have.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Mark|15|15|text=And so Pilate, willing to '''content''' the people, released Barabbas unto them, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.}}
#* {{RQ:Watts Improvement|14|194|text=Do not '''content''' yourselves with meer Words and Names, lest your laboured Improvements only amass a heap of unintelligible Phrases, and you feed upon Husks instead of Kernels.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Felicity Cloake|title=How to make the perfect cacio e pepe|date=3 November 2016|url=https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/wordofmouth/2016/nov/03/how-to-make-the-perfect-cacio-e-pepe
|passage=Caz Hildebrand and Jacob Kenedy recommend rigatoni in the Geometry of Pasta, and Christopher Boswell, the chef behind the Rome Sustainable Food project, prefers wholemeal paccheri or rigatoni in his book Pasta, on the basis that “the flavour of the whole grain is strong enough to stand up to the sharp and salty sheep’s milk cheese” (as I can find neither easily, I have to '''content''' myself with brown penne instead).|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261026113423/https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/wordofmouth/2016/nov/03/how-to-make-the-perfect-cacio-e-pepe|archivedate=26 October 2026}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To satisfy the expectations of; to pay; to [[requite]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 3|III|2|text=Come the next Sabbath, and I will '''content''' you.}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|content}} (plural {{m|enm|contentes}}, {{m|enm|contence}}), from {{der|en|la|contentus}}, past participle of {{m|la|continēre||to hold in, contain}}, as Etymology 1, above. English apparently developed a substantive form of the adjective, which is not mirrored in Romance languages.

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɒn.tɛnt/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-content (noun).wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɔn.tɛnt/|a=UK}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-content.wav|a=London}}
* {{enPR|kŏn'tĕnt|a=GA,CA}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑn.tɛnt/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-content.ogg|a=California}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔntɛnt|ɒntɛnt|ɑntɛnt|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|con|tent}}

====Adjective====
{{en-adj}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[contained|Contained]].

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} That which is [[contain]]ed.
#: {{syn|en|contents}}
# {{senseid|en|semantic information}} Subject matter; [[semantic]] information (or a portion or body thereof); that which is contained in [[writing]], [[speech]], [[video]], etc.
#: {{ux|en|Although eloquently delivered, the '''content''' of the speech was objectionable.}}
#: {{ux|en|You can look up the chapter on special relativity in the table of '''contents'''.}}
## {{lb|en|by extension|uncountable}} One or more [[creative work]]s.
##: {{ux|en|Some online video creators upload new '''content''' every day.}}
##: {{ux|en|Prolific creators manage their voluminous '''content''' with any of various content management systems.}}
### {{lb|en|internet|colloquial}} The [[potential]] of creative work for a [[content creator]].
###: {{ux|en|He moved to California for the '''content'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Dickens Barnaby Rudge|chapter=21|passage=Hugh admitting that he never had, and moreover that he couldn’t read, Mrs Varden declared with much severity, that he ought to he even more ashamed of himself than before, and strongly recommended him to save up his pocket-money for the purchase of one, and further to teach himself the '''contents''' with all convenient diligence.}}
#* {{RQ:Wired|author=w:John Perry Barlow|year=2000|month=October|title=The Next Economy Of Ideas|url=https://www.wired.com/2000/10/download/|passage=In the future, instead of bottles of dead "'''content'''," I imagine electronically defined venues, where minds residing in bodies scattered all over the planet are admitted, either by subscription or a ticket at a time, into the real-time presence of the creative act.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260813061456/https://www.wired.com/2000/10/download/|archivedate=13 August 2026}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman|volume=189|issue=2|page=27|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly|title=The tao of tech|url=https://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google|passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about "creating compelling '''content'''", or{{...}}and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261026113327/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google|archivedate=26 October 2026}}
# The amount of material contained.
#: {{ux|en|Light beer has a lower alcohol '''content''' than regular beer.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[capacity|Capacity]] for containing.
#* {{RQ:Bacon New Atlantis|passage=Strong ships, of great '''content'''.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics}} The [[n-dimensional|''n''-dimensional]] space contained by an ''n''-dimensional [[polytope]] (called ''[[volume]]'' in the case of a [[polyhedron]] and ''[[area]]'' in the case of a [[polygon]]); length, area or volume, generalized to an arbitrary number of dimensions. {{C|en|Higher-dimensional geometry}}
# {{lb|en|algebra|ring theory|of a [[polynomial]] with coefficients in a [[GCD domain]]}} The [[greatest common divisor]] of the [[coefficient]]s; {{lb|en|of a polynomial with coefficients in an [[integral domain]]}} the common factor of the coefficients which, when removed, leaves the adjusted coefficients with no common factor that is [[noninvertible]].

=====Usage notes=====
* Sense 2.1 can be seen as denigrating due to its association with [[monetization]], terms such as {{m|en|content farm}}, and sense 2.1.1. See also {{m|en|slop}}.
